name: royal street lamp, 3/4 top-down: square stone pedestal (top face seen from above, front face with a small blue plaque), dark iron post with gold bands, curled iron brackets, an octagonal lantern with warm lit glass and a gold crown cap
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_lamp

answer.evidence: The pedestal (rows 36-45, 12 wide) is the main body. Rows 36-40 are a light top face with a lighter rim at row 36. A darker line at rows 41-42 marks its front edge and eave shadow. Below that is a front face of about 5 rows (rows 41-45) with the blue plaque. The lantern has a stepped roof that widens from 3 to 11 px over rows 2-7 and ends in a gold eave band at rows 6-7, so it reads as a roof plane. The thin post has no top, which is correct for a 3-px shaft.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has 18 visible tones per 16x16 tile, level with the detailed references (stall 17, well 20) and well above the hedge (9). Near-flat coverage is 0%, so there are no flat fills. The pedestal shows a lit top face, a shaded front and a plaque. The lantern has a glass gradient and a gold cap. The post carries gold bands and brackets, so the thin silhouette is not a plain one-colour line like the crook lamp. About 59% of dark edge pixels are near-neutral. That is expected on dark iron, and the stone and gold edges look tinted, so I call the outline mixed rather than a uniform black sticker line. It has about 4 steps per material against the references' 5-6, and its 24 total colours are below the larger props. For a thin prop that is acceptable, and it is clearly richer than the crook lamp reference. A careful artist would accept it next to the references.

answer.evidence: The pedestal is 12 px wide. Rows 36-41 are a light top face (L about 200-230) that ends in a darker front-edge line at row 42. The lantern has a stepped pyramid roof (widths 3, 5, 7, 9, 11 on rows 2-6) over a gold eave band at rows 6-7, with a darker edge at row 7; this counts as a roof plane. The post is a thin 3 px shaft and the lantern glass is a vertical face. The roof widens and then ends flat on a narrower body, so it is a hat and not an ellipse cap.

answer.evidence: The pedestal (rows 36-45, 12 px wide) is the main body. Its light stone top spans rows 36-40/41 (L about 221, widening from the 5 px post base at row 35). Darker rows 41-42 mark the front edge, and the front face with the blue plaque spans rows 42-45. The lantern roof (rows 2-7) is a stepped pyramid, 3 px wide widening to 11 px. It reads as a sloped roof plane over a gold eave at rows 6-7, flat at the bottom, so it is not an ellipse cap. The lantern glass (rows 8-13) and the thin post are vertical faces.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate carries 18 visible tones per full tile, against 17 for the cheese stall and 20 for the roofed well. It is far above the lamp-crook and bench references, which measure 0 because they are thin. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so the pedestal, post and lantern show no large flat fills. The pedestal has a lit top face, a mid front face and a darker side, and the lantern glass and gold crown add several warm steps, giving about 4 distinct steps per material. The outline is mixed: 59% of dark edge pixels are neutral, but the iron post is naturally dark, and the Beodeul lamp-crook reference is itself 100% neutral. The 24 total colours are plausible for a narrow prop, richer than the 14-colour lamp-crook and bench. It would sit next to the references without looking thinner or more sticker-like, though the shading is slightly shallower than the roofed well or stall.
